brief.summary: Front-end and long-end yields are described as biased higher, with long yields near multi-decade highs; equity futures are slightly softer but near records. The dollar is up as the euro falls to a 17-month low, oil is higher, and gold and credit spreads were not discussed. The Fed is seen as potentially hiking, though John Williams sounds less hawkish and markets lack a clear reaction function; Powell faces political pressure. The dominant narrative is a global bond selloff centered on French debt, offset by resilient AI earnings and equity highs. Geopolitics is escalating around Yemen and Iran, while the consumer is weak on cost-of-living. The show’s net tone is neutral.
notable_quotes: I can't control the bond market. What I can do is get people to slow down and think.
Bonds selling off on weak data was the story into the weekend.
